static_traits.name: Lin Ruowei
static_traits.occupation: Restaurant employee and cupcake business owner
static_traits.family_status: Married with children, responsible for driving children to school
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues strained due to lateness; spouse supportive but support limited
static_traits.medical_history: No history of psychotherapy in the past; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, neutral tone but with a sense of frustration; often using absolute statements (such as 'never possible to be on time')

basic_info.main_problem: I always feel I can never be on time, because after dropping the children at school I am always late for work, which causes stress and guilt.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because persistent lateness has affected my work performance and caused stress in my personal life.
growth_experiences: Started working at a restaurant after having children; mornings require dropping children at school first, then rushing to the work site. Over time, commute traffic congestion and rushed morning preparations increased lateness frequency, with stress and guilt constantly accumulating, affecting self-esteem and interaction with colleagues; although the spouse is supportive and helps when feasible, work constraints make the support insufficient to solve the problem.

core_beliefs: I can never be on time

special_situations.event: After dropping the child at school in the morning, encounters commuting congestion, causing being late for work check-in
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot meet the time demands of both family and work, it means I am irresponsible / a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets multiple alarms, optimizes the morning schedule, speeds up the pace to squeeze time
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never be on time

special_situations.event: The boss showed dissatisfaction over lateness, work performance affected
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are dissatisfied with me, it means I am an irresponsible person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Guilt and self-blame; works overtime or completes tasks faster to compensate
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I am irresponsible / not committed

special_situations.event: Preparing to discuss adjusting work hours with the boss, but unsure whether the other will agree
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the boss does not agree, I have no way to solve the problem and will always be late
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hesitant and indecisive, repeatedly weighing and delaying action
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She probably will not agree, this plan will not work

special_situations.event: Before leaving home already feels highly rushed and tense, worrying the morning routine will be disrupted
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the start is not perfect, everything after will collapse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Cramming more tasks into limited time, constantly speeding up to 'beat the clock'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It will be late again today; everything will go wrong

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as reliable while competently filling both mother and employee roles
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as irresponsible by boss and colleagues, being blamed or affecting work stability; fearing being unable to take good care of the children
defense_goal: Maintaining order and reducing guilt through doubled control and self-harshness
Avoiding directly facing the possibility of being rejected to lower anxiety

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing taking action (such as communicating with the boss to adjust work hours) or being judged by others for being late
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Generalizing the boss's dissatisfaction into others negating oneself, subjectively concluding 'they think I am irresponsible'.
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopting a gentle, empathic tone, acknowledging the worries, while moderately challenging the assumptions; using open-ended questions to guide concretizing the worries, and encouraging small-step attempts.

manifestations: After childbirth, she takes on both parenting and work roles; morning time is constrained by external arrangements and transportation, making it hard to control
Highly attached to the value condition of 'must be on time', feels bound by rules and responsibilities
Uncertain and concerned about options like adjusting work hours or using the school bus

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Subjectively concluding colleagues think one is irresponsible / not committed
Assuming the boss will not agree to adjusting work hours

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame and guilt, attributes being late to character problems
Constantly self-scrutinizing and speeding up in the morning, trying to 'beat the clock'

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Emphasizes 'I must be on time' and 'I should care for the children well and arrive at work on time'
Evaluates self-worth with absolutist rules, leading to increased pressure and guilt

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse helping with childcare
Willing to try communicating with the boss to adjust hours
Has already tried multiple strategies (setting alarms, optimizing schedule, seeking help)
Has the ability to analyze rationally and evaluate options
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking, predicting the future, catastrophizing and other cognitive biases present
Overly focused on others' evaluations, worrying about being seen as irresponsible
Morning time structure and commuting environment constraints (school drop-off and traffic congestion)
Guilt and stress accumulating over the long term, impaired self-esteem

antecedent: Taking kids to school in the morning
Already feeling rushed and tense before leaving home
target_behavior.core_reason: In the conflict between family and work roles, time management constrained along with the catastrophic/absolute cognition of 'I can never be on time'
target_behavior.function: Prioritizing childcare tasks for short-term reassurance, temporarily escaping the anxiety of being judged
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance affected, boss dissatisfied, tense relationships with colleagues; stress and guilt intensified, impaired self-esteem

antecedent: Insufficient preparation before leaving or time pressure
Anticipating traffic congestion and lateness risk
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white belief in 'must be perfectly on time' and predicting negative future outcomes
target_behavior.function: Drives action by raising arousal (self-stimulation/mobilization), but causes inefficiency and chaos
target_behavior.consequence: Plans are chaotic, time consumption increases; lateness worsens and high tension is maintained all day
